assumptions: Search-space complexity can be proxy-measured by node divergence in a simulation.
High-value scientific problems generate divergent pathways rather than linear paths.
Epistemic gain is correlated with the information entropy of the generated solution tree.
definition.falsification: If the prioritized problems consistently show low path divergence across multiple synthetic problem spaces, the hypothesis is falsified.
definition.statement: An agent can autonomously evaluate the quality of a potential scientific problem by calculating the ratio of search-space exploration to the divergence of generated solution nodes; problems with high divergence relative to exploration cost are prioritized as high-value.
definition.uncertainty: The primary uncertainty is whether path divergence is a sufficient surrogate for epistemic significance in open-ended inquiry.

definition.method: Execute a comparative search over synthetic problem graphs, measuring the ratio of leaf-node divergence to the total number of explored branches. Use this ratio to rank problem candidates against a set of 'known' high-value problem structures.
definition.success: The agent must rank problem p1 as the highest value due to its optimal divergence/cost ratio.
